subject: Workplace Skills
title: Trust by Default
description: A micro-lesson that makes Trust by Default usable.

hook.text: Some managers install tracking software to monitor keystrokes. Their best employees quit within six months.

buildup.text: Surveillance signals distrust. When people feel watched, they perform tasks but stop thinking creatively.

discovery.text: High-performing remote teams operate on trust by default. They measure output, not hours or keystrokes.

twist.text: Trust doesn't mean no accountability. It means clear expectations and regular check-ins, not surveillance.

climax.text: Set clear deliverables and deadlines. Trust people to manage their own time to hit them.

punchline.text: Measure output, not activity. Trust follows clarity.

quiz.question: Why does employee monitoring often backfire in remote settings?
options: The software is too expensive for most companies
Surveillance signals distrust and kills creative thinking
Employees can easily trick monitoring tools
